newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks dip at opening, look to U.S..
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks dip at opening, look to U.S..

text.p: Australian shares slipped at the opening on Friday as the market took a tentative attitude ahead of U.S. employment data due later in the day.
The All Ordinaries index dipped 8.40 points to 2,439.0.
Brokers said the cautious tone was likely to set the stage for a day of rangebound trading with few investors prepared to commit ahead of the weekend.

"Bonds were off from the start but I think it is more that no-one wants to move in ahead of the weekend," said a Sydney broker. "Employment numbers are due out in the States later today and we are likely to stay hesitant ahead of that."
Others echoed similar sentiment, noting that a holiday weekend in Victoria was likely to further diminish interest.
"We might well see the Friday afternoon effect, particularly going into a long weekend," said a Melbourne-based dealer.
Bakery and milling group Goodman Fielder reported a 22 percent rise in first half net profit to A$55.8 million (US$43.94 million), pushing its shares a cent higher to A$1.61.
Rises barely shaded falls while about 41 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
